title: Prospective analysis of microbial associations and dynamic changes between the root canal, apical region, subgingival crevicular fluid, saliva and blood during endodontic retreatment in persistent apical periodontitis
summary:
Inflammation at the tip of a tooth root can persist even after root canal treatment. The reasons why these inflammations do not heal in some patients are not yet fully understood. One possible explanation is a remaining bacterial burden or a specific composition of bacteria inside the tooth.
Chronic inflammation is not limited to one part of the body. Inflammation in the oral cavity may, similar to inflammation in other organs, influence overall health. Previous studies have reported associations between persistent inflammation and systemic diseases, such as cardiovascular conditions.
The aim of this study is to investigate how the bacterial composition in the tooth and oral cavity changes during endodontic retreatment and how these changes are reflected in the blood. This approach is intended to improve the understanding of potential interactions between local dental inflammation and systemic health.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Age ≥ 18 years and ability to provide informed consent.
Presence of clinical symptoms such as pain, swelling, recurrent infections, purulent discharge, or tooth mobility.
Evidence of an inadequate previous root canal treatment performed more than 6 months prior (e.g. incomplete root canal filling or missed root canals).
Radiographically detectable periapical lesion associated with a previously root canal–treated tooth.
The affected tooth is considered restorable based on clinical and restorative assessment.
Written informed consent obtained prior to participation.
Exclusion criteria:
Non-restorable teeth, for example due to vertical root fractures, severe marginal attachment loss, severely obliterated root canals, or the presence of fractured instruments.
Age < 18 years or inability to provide informed consent.
Severely curved roots or anatomical conditions that substantially impede standardized endodontic retreatment.
Compromised endodontic retreatment due to severely obliterated root canals or fractured instruments within the root canal system.
Endodontic retreatment of mandibular premolars and mandibular anterior teeth.
